overview.body:
**Taaroa** ​(*taaroa*) ‌— Creator, ‌Supreme ​Being ​· ​The distant ​one ​— ‌belongs ​to the ​Polynesian ‌tradition, ​where it ‌is ​catalogued ‌under ​the domain ​"Creator, ​Supreme ​Being". ​The name ‌means ​"The ‌distant ​one".

**Taaroa** ‌is ​creator, ‌supreme ​being. The ‌name ​means ​"The ‌distant one" ‌and ‌belongs ​to the ​polynesian ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores the ‌name ​as ​**Taaroa** ‌and serves ​its ‌temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/taaroa/). ​The ​restoration ‌needs ‌no distinctive ​letters ‌or ​diacritics its ​ASCII ‌form ‌would ‌lose, which ‌places ​the ‌name ​in Tier ​2. ​The ‌plain ​ASCII form ​*taaroa* ​survives ‌as ​a modern ​convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in ​modern Polynesian ​orthographies; ​macron usage ​follows ​each ‌tradition’s reference ​dictionaries. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "The ‌distant ​one".

‌The ASCII ​form ​*taaroa* survives ​only ​because ​the early ‌domain-name ​system could ‌not ​carry ‌diacritics; it ​is ‌a technological ​compromise, ‌not ​an ancient ​spelling. ‌The Unicode ‌restoration ‌**Taaroa** recovers ​the ​full ‌diacritic detail ​of ​the scholarly ‌transliteration ​directly ​in the ‌address ​bar. The ‌restoration ​needs ​no distinctive ​letters ​or diacritics ‌its ‌ASCII ​form would ‌lose, ​which places ​the ‌name in ‌Tier ‌2.

‌The letter-by-letter ​transformation ‌runs:

- ​**t** ​→ ​**T** — ‌Same, ​capitalized
- ​**a** ​→ ‌**a** — ​Same
​- **a** ​→ ‌**a** ​— Same
‌- ​**r** → ‌**r** ​— Same
‌- ‌**o** ​→ **o** ​— ​Same
- ​**a** ‌→ ‌**a** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/taaroa/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**taaroa** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Taaroa.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"taaroa" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Taaroa".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"taaroa" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Taaroa" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Taaroa was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Taaroa ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Taaroa ‌place ​creator, supreme ​being ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

### ‌Origins ​(Myth)

‌Taaroa appears ​in ‌polynesian tradition ​as ​creator, ​supreme being. ​The ​name's meaning, ‌"The ​distant ‌one", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ‌this ​figure.

### ‌Worship ​and Memory ​(Cult)

‌Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ​preserved Taaroa ​in ‌ritual, ​text, and ​iconography, ‌ensuring the ​name ​survived ‌into the ​modern ‌scholarly ​record.

The ​myths ​of Taaroa ​survive ‌in ‌fragments, summaries, ​and ‌later retellings. ​Each ​version ‌reflects the ‌interests ‌of its ‌tellers ​— ‌poets, priests, ​philosophers, ​and scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; ​it gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Taaroa ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Taaroa ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Polynesian ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Taaroa, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​creator ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Taaroa is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​creator, ​Supreme ‌Being ​in the ​mind ‌and ​to ‌ask ​what of ‌it ​endures. ​The ​name means ​"The ​distant ‌one" ​— and ‌a ​name ‌that ​carries its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly ​invites meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as creator, ‌Supreme ​Being ​· ‌The distant ​one.

‌Sit ​with ​the restored ​form ​— ‌Taaroa ‌— and ​the ‌diacritics ​themselves ​become ‌the practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, ​a refusal ‌to ​let ​the ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*taaroa* ​stand ​in for ‌the ​whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
